name: Amina Raza
quote: I want every painting to feel like a small window into the stories and places that shaped us.
bio: Amina works with layered pigments, fine brushes and regional motifs. Her studio practice brings together folk memory, landscape and the patient detail of hand-painted surfaces. Each piece is developed by hand, with careful attention to colour balance, texture and the small irregularities that make handmade art individual.

name: Sanaullah Qadri
quote: For me, a beautiful letter is both a form and a feeling.
bio: Sanaullah studies the rhythm of traditional scripts and the relationship between line, space and meaning. His practice combines disciplined lettering with considered composition, preparing each work slowly so that the written form remains the centre of the piece.

name: Mehwish Bano
quote: Jewellery should carry a memory while still feeling natural to wear.
bio: Mehwish creates wearable pieces by combining careful hand assembly, traditional ornament references and modern everyday proportions. She selects materials for their finish and comfort, then checks each clasp and detail before a piece leaves her worktable.

name: Ustad Javed Hussain
quote: Clay teaches patience. The hands learn something new with every piece.
bio: Javed learned to read clay through touch, moisture and movement. His process moves from preparing the clay to shaping, drying and finishing each form. Small variations in curve and glaze are part of the character of a hand-shaped vessel.

name: Rashida Parveen
quote: I make things that bring warmth to the spaces people call home.
bio: Rashida draws inspiration from domestic craft traditions, natural textures and the way objects make a room feel welcoming. She plans each decorative piece around practical use, balanced colour and a finish that can be enjoyed every day.

name: Bilal Ahmed
quote: A sculpture should invite people to look twice and discover another detail.
bio: Bilal explores volume, balance and tactile surfaces through hand-shaped forms. He begins with a simple sketch, studies the material and refines the silhouette gradually. His work celebrates the expressive quality of objects made slowly by hand.

name: Hina Khalid
quote: Small details can make an ordinary day feel special.
bio: Hina transforms fabric, thread and decorative details into comfortable accessories. She pays special attention to secure finishing, gentle edges and colour combinations that complement both festive and everyday clothing.

name: Nadia Akhtar
quote: The charm of a jhumka is in the movement and the hand-finished detail.
bio: Nadia specialises in traditional jhumka forms, balancing ornament, movement and wearability. Each design is assembled and finished with care, drawing on familiar South Asian silhouettes while allowing each pair its own character.

name: Farzana Bibi
quote: A good pair of khusas should feel as special as the occasion.
bio: Farzana works with traditional footwear construction, decorative stitching and careful shaping. She focuses on a comfortable fit and durable finishing, bringing regional patterns into footwear that can be worn for celebrations and everyday occasions.

name: Omar Farooq
quote: Fragrance is a quiet signature, remembered long after a moment has passed.
bio: Omar develops fragrance blends by considering their opening notes, heart and lasting base. His small-batch approach values balance and restraint, with careful bottling and presentation for people who enjoy traditional fragrance rituals.

name: Sajid Malik
quote: Light is part of the material. I design each piece with that in mind.
bio: Sajid explores transparency, colour and light through decorative glass craft. His process considers how a piece looks in daylight and under warm indoor lighting, with careful attention to smooth edges and a clean final finish.

name: Noreen Yousaf
quote: Every stitch is time, care and a little piece of the maker.
bio: Noreen builds each textile form stitch by stitch, selecting yarn weight, texture and construction for the intended use. Her work values consistency without losing the warmth and individuality of handmade crochet and knitting.
